title: [E9] Implement: Native bundled WireGuard pool lifecycle and readiness enforcement
description:
Scope:
- Add native runtime support for bundled Surfshark wireproxy assets so the benchmark and probe do not just read manifests, but can ensure the local proxy pool is actually runnable and ready.
- Detect missing wireproxy binaries, dead localhost proxy endpoints, stale pid files, and failed startup before benchmark execution begins.
- Reuse one shared readiness path for both the Tesla benchmark CLI and the wireproxy domain probe CLI.

Why:
- The current bundled WireGuard path only converts manifest entries into proxy URLs like http://127.0.0.1:29xxx and socks5h://127.0.0.1:19xxx. It never starts the local wireproxy pool, so the benchmark can fail the entire rotation sweep in seconds with local-access-health-quarantine even when partner domains were never actually reached.
- We need a precise, reliable native solution, not a manual workaround or tribal-knowledge startup sequence.
design:
Design Notes:
- The runtime should own preflight and startup logic, not the user.
- Prefer explicit readiness verification over optimistic startup assumptions.
- If the bundled asset manifest exposes start/stop scripts, use them as lifecycle hooks for the asset bundle, but surface a typed, actionable error when wireproxy is not installed or the selected entries do not become reachable.
- Readiness should be entry-aware so rotation mode can verify only the exits it intends to use.
- Avoid silently degrading to direct traffic or to a dead proxy list.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bundled wireproxy execution fails fast with an explicit actionable error when the wireproxy binary is missing.
- Bundled wireproxy execution can start the pool automatically when required entries are not ready and a start script is available.
- Benchmark and probe CLIs share the same readiness path before creating access modules.
- Deterministic tests cover missing binary, dead-entry readiness failure, and successful readiness verification/startup orchestration.
notes:
Closed after two blind reviews (Epicurus the 2nd, Raman the 2nd) confirmed the diagnosis and the current readiness behavior. Current workspace evidence:
- Tesla benchmark with bundled WireGuard now fails immediately and explicitly when `wireproxy` is unavailable instead of producing a misleading 13-second artifact.
- Explicit-binary probe via `WIREPROXY_BIN=/Users/satan/code/trading-agent/trading_workspace/us_equities_watchlist/bin/wireproxy` succeeded 8/8 on example.com and 14/16 on Alza/Datart, proving the bundled configs and readiness/startup path are operational when the host supplies a real binary.
- Remaining variability is now remote/exit-quality behavior (for example 403 on Alza for some exits, timeout on `de_frankfurt-am-main_10fe4eca` for Datart), not the old dead-pool benchmark pathology.
close_reason: Readiness enforcement verified; remaining issues are host binary/exit quality, not benchmark infra

title: E9 Truth-Aware Content Correctness and Benchmark Intelligence
description:
Scope:
- Extend the completed E9 benchmark and parity work from access-focused evidence into truth-aware content correctness for Tesla partner pages.
- Add partner-specific ground truth and policy-driven scoring for title, price, and description so the system can distinguish access success from output correctness.
- Turn benchmark evidence into adaptive runtime behavior, explainable diagnostics, curation assets, and recovery intelligence.
- Break the program into standalone workstreams with explicit dependency wiring so parallel agents can execute it safely and future reviewers can understand the intent without rediscovering the context.

Background:
- The current Tesla partner benchmark proves useful access/runtime signals, but it still lacks a first-class model for true output correctness on partner pages.
- Exact string equality is too strict for partner titles and descriptions, while access-only metrics are too weak to detect wrong-product or low-quality-content success states.
- The real Tesla datasets already contain richer identity hints such as model tokens and accessory signals; the current wrapper and artifact model discard most of that value.
- This epic exists to convert E9 from a benchmark that mostly answers “did we reach the page?” into one that can answer “did we return the correct, usable product output with evidence and the right operational strategy?”
design:
Design Notes:
- Separate product identity truth from partner snapshot truth. Identity truth answers whether the page is the right product; partner snapshot truth answers what the partner page actually showed at a particular time.
- Keep the frozen corpus artifact lean. Add richer expectation and truth metadata through a sidecar expectation artifact or equivalent join model instead of bloating the access-oriented corpus page contract.
- Prefer deterministic scoring over opaque heuristics. Fuzzy title matching, price tolerance, and description quality should be explicit, reviewable, and explainable.
- Treat price and description truth as time-sensitive. Staleness and capture time are core parts of the model, not incidental metadata.
- Reuse the existing extraction, normalization, observation, reference-pack, and benchmark stack where possible. The point is to increase system leverage, not create a disconnected subsystem.
- Make every new benchmark artifact tell a better story: access result, extracted content, truth comparison, evidence, and next recommended action.
- Ensure the backlog supports phased delivery. Foundational schema and scoring work should unblock benchmark integration, explainability, adaptive runtime behavior, and pack improvement loops.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- A partner-specific truth model exists for title, price, and description, including freshness and validation policy metadata.
- Benchmark and parity artifacts publish field-level correctness, not only access/runtime success.
- The runtime can use content-aware signals to decide escalation and produce explainable diagnostics for failures and low-confidence outputs.
- Counterexamples and strong successes can be converted into curation inputs and pack-improvement proposals.
- End-to-end documentation and capability-slice evidence explain how this work improves the system’s usefulness, reliability, and operational leverage.

title: [E9] Task: Implement content-aware gate evaluation and reporting
description:
Scope:
- Implement the gate evaluation logic and expose verdict rationale through benchmark reports and summaries.
- Ensure the gate layer uses the structured artifact outputs instead of duplicating underlying scoring logic.

Why:
- A policy that is not encoded into the benchmark verdict path will drift into documentation-only intent.
design:
Design Notes:
- Keep verdict rationale machine-readable and reviewable.
- Preserve backward compatibility where possible, but prioritize semantic clarity.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmark outputs include content-aware verdicts and rationale.
- Regression tests prove the gate layer responds correctly to representative content-success and access-only cases.

title: [E9] Implement: Content-aware benchmark gates and verdict rules
description:
Scope:
- Define and implement how truth-aware content signals change benchmark pass, warn, and fail semantics at the attempt, sweep, and suite levels.
- Separate transport success from content success so the benchmark can make trustworthy gating decisions.

Why:
- Without an explicit gate layer, the new scoring and reporting stack still leaves the benchmark’s headline verdict anchored to access success.
- Users need the benchmark to tell them not only what happened, but whether that result should block, warn, or pass.
design:
Design Notes:
- Gate semantics should use explicit field coverage thresholds, freshness handling, and content-success criteria rather than ad hoc report interpretation.
- Keep the first version deterministic and reviewable.
- The gate layer should consume benchmark artifacts rather than duplicating extraction logic.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmark verdict rules distinguish access-only success from content-success and identity-valid success.
- Sweep and suite verdicts can be driven by explicit content-aware thresholds.
- Reports make the new gate semantics legible to operators and reviewers.

title: [E9] Task: Define content-success thresholds and sweep verdict policy
description:
Scope:
- Define required-field coverage, identity prerequisites, freshness treatment, and score thresholds for benchmark pass, warn, and fail decisions.
- Specify how missing truth coverage affects verdict strength.

Why:
- The benchmark cannot become truth-aware until its verdict semantics are explicit and reviewable.
design:
Design Notes:
- Distinguish hard gates from soft scorecards.
- Make policy visible enough that future changes require explicit review.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- A documented policy exists for attempt, sweep, and suite verdicts under truth-aware benchmarking.
- Missing truth, stale truth, and identity-failed cases have explicit handling.

title: [E9] Verify: Adaptive escalation uplift and safety envelope
description:
Scope:
- Verify that adaptive escalation improves content outcomes in the intended cases without causing unacceptable browser-cost growth or obvious false-escalation patterns.
- Document the safety envelope for the first rollout.

Why:
- Escalation is a leverage feature, but it is also one of the easiest places to add hidden cost and complexity.
design:
Design Notes:
- Compare representative no-escalation, useful-escalation, ambiguous, and low-yield cases.
- Use the verification output to define safe rollout expectations rather than relying on intuition.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Verification demonstrates when escalation helps, when it does not, and what the cost trade-off looks like.
- The first-rollout safety envelope is explicit and reviewable.

title: [E9] Verify: Scorer contract and ambiguity matrix
description:
Scope:
- Verify the scorer contract, reason codes, and ambiguity handling against curated examples of correct, acceptable, mismatched, stale, and identity-failed outputs.
- Ensure downstream consumers can rely on stable semantics across fields.

Why:
- The scoring engine is the semantic core of the whole initiative; if its edge cases drift, everything above it becomes noisy or misleading.
design:
Design Notes:
- Focus on representative ambiguity cases, not just ideal positives and obvious negatives.
- Prefer reviewable tables of expected outcomes so policy changes are explicit.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Verification covers representative title, price, and description ambiguity cases plus identity-failed outcomes.
- Reason codes and outcome states are stable and documented enough for downstream consumers.

title: [E9] Verify: Truth-based parity correctness matrix
description:
Scope:
- Verify that fixture and live parity reporting cleanly separates ours-vs-truth, Scrapling-vs-truth, and mutual agreement without correctness.
- Confirm that parity outputs do not accidentally treat shared wrongness as success.

Why:
- The parity retrofit only delivers value if it changes the meaning of comparison, not just the shape of the report.
design:
Design Notes:
- Use a small matrix of representative cases where agreement and correctness diverge.
- Keep outputs explicit enough that a reviewer can explain each verdict.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Verification proves parity reports distinguish correctness from mutual agreement.
- Representative fixtures or live-style cases document the expected outcome matrix.

title: [E9] Verify: Benchmark artifact and wrapper content summaries
description:

- Ensure existing consumers degrade safely and new consumers can trust the richer fields.

Why:
- Artifact schema changes are only useful if they are coherent, stable, and operationally readable.
design:
Design Notes:
- Verify both schema-level stability and human-readable usefulness.
- Include representative cases with missing truth, stale truth, identity failure, and clean success.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Verification proves artifacts carry the intended structured fields and readable summaries.
- Representative cases show that content and identity results are actionable during triage.

title: [E9] Verify: Dataset and expectation compatibility matrix
description:
Scope:
- Verify the schema and loader layer against the known Tesla dataset variants, enrichment cases, stale-truth inputs, and partial-coverage inputs.
- Produce a compatibility matrix that future maintainers can use as the ground truth for supported dataset shapes.

Why:
- This feature will be a long-lived ingestion boundary; unsupported shape drift must be caught deliberately, not discovered during benchmark runs.
design:
Design Notes:
- Cover both happy-path compatibility and failure-path diagnostics.
- Preserve a reviewable matrix of representative inputs rather than only unit-level microcases.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- A compatibility matrix exists for legacy, strict, enriched, partial, and stale truth inputs.
- Verification proves loader diagnostics are actionable and deterministic.

title: [E9] Task: Add escalation guardrails cost budgets and effectiveness telemetry
description:
Scope:
- Add explicit telemetry around when escalation happened, what it cost, and whether it improved content correctness.
- Encode simple guardrails so adaptive escalation can be tuned without accidentally exploding browser cost or masking low-yield strategies.

Why:
- A smarter escalation policy is only valuable if operators can see whether it paid off.
- Without cost and uplift telemetry, the system could become more complex while getting harder to trust.
design:
Design Notes:
- Capture both incremental cost and incremental content gain.
- Prefer lightweight, reviewable guardrails over opaque optimization logic.
- Make the telemetry reusable by later scorecards and recovery recommendations.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Escalation telemetry exposes frequency, cost, and content-uplift signals.
- Guardrails prevent silent policy drift toward runaway browser usage.
- Reports make it possible to evaluate whether adaptive escalation is earning its complexity.

title: [E9] Integrate: Minimum viable truth-aware Tesla partner capability slice
description:

- Explicitly exclude second-wave optimization and auto-pack proposal features from the MVP slice so foundational value can ship earlier.

Why:

- Users get the biggest value jump from seeing access, identity, content correctness, and evidence in one flow; recommendation and automation layers can follow.
design:
Design Notes:

- The goal is typed boundary compatibility, reproducible execution, and evidence that the combined system delivers more value than the access-only baseline.
acceptance_criteria:

- Integration evidence shows access, identity, content scoring, and diagnostics working together.
- The slice is strong enough to serve as the baseline for later optimization and pack-evolution work.

acceptance_criteria:

- Mutual agreement alone can no longer produce a false sense of correctness.

acceptance_criteria:

acceptance_criteria:

title: [E9] Implement: Adaptive access-to-content escalation
description:
Scope:
- Add a cheap post-fetch content probe so HTTP success is re-evaluated before a page is considered done.
- Escalate to browser or alternate strategies when required content is missing, low-confidence, or identity-suspicious.
- Measure whether escalation improves correctness enough to justify its added cost.

Why:
- The current pipeline can treat HTTP-first access success as “good enough” even when content correctness is weak.
- Adaptive escalation improves both quality and efficiency by escalating only when content evidence justifies the cost.
design:
Design Notes:
- Escalation policy should consume shared scorer and identity signals.
- The runtime must distinguish access failure, content failure, and ambiguity so later optimizers can learn from them.
- Preserve cost-awareness: do not escalate everything just because a richer scoring system exists.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- HTTP-first success no longer bypasses content checks for required fields.
- Escalation decisions are driven by explicit scorer and identity outputs and are visible in artifacts.
- Deterministic tests and telemetry cover escalate, do-not-escalate, ambiguous, and low-yield cases.

title: [E9] Implement: Field-level evidence explainability and counterexample harvesting
description:
Scope:
- Emit explainable evidence bundles for each field so operators can see raw value, normalized value, selector path, truth comparison, and mismatch reason.
- Capture benchmark failures and low-confidence outputs into a reusable counterexample stream for future curation and regression testing.

Why:
- A truth-aware system that cannot explain itself will still feel opaque and hard to trust.
- Counterexamples are the fastest path to making the benchmark and packs improve in the places that actually matter.
- This is core operator leverage, not optional polish.
design:
Design Notes:
- Evidence should be compact enough for routine inspection but structured enough for automation.
- Harvested counterexamples should include enough context to become fixture candidates or pack proposals without manual archaeology.
- Reuse existing evidence and snapshot concepts rather than inventing a separate debug-only format.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Field-level explanations are emitted in artifacts or adjacent evidence outputs.
- Counterexamples can be collected from live benchmark runs with enough structured context for review.
- Diagnostics clearly separate identity errors, extraction errors, policy mismatches, and stale-truth ambiguity, so operators can take the right next action.

title: [E9] Implement: Truth-based parity retrofit for fixture and live comparisons
description:
Scope:
- Replace parity logic that mainly compares Effect-Scrapling against Scrapling with parity logic that compares both systems against ground truth and then against each other.
- Upgrade live parity to use tolerant title matching and partner-specific policies instead of exact normalized string equality.

Why:
- Mutual agreement is not correctness. Two systems can agree on the wrong answer.
- This feature makes parity an actual quality measure instead of a similarity measure.
design:
Design Notes:
- Preserve ours-vs-scrapling comparisons as a diagnostic, but do not let them stand in for truth.
- Live parity should remain policy-driven and explainable, especially for titles and descriptions.
- Reuse the shared scoring engine rather than embedding new ad hoc comparisons.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Fixture and live parity artifacts record ours-vs-truth, scrapling-vs-truth, and ours-vs-scrapling signals.
- Live parity no longer depends on brittle exact title equality as the main correctness gate.
- Parity artifacts include enough diagnostics to explain disagreements and ambiguous cases.

title: [E9] Implement: Product identity guardrail layer
description:
Scope:
- Add a dedicated identity guardrail that decides whether a fetched partner page belongs to the intended Tesla product before downstream field correctness is trusted.
- Use model tokens, variant handling, accessory classification, and forbidden-token rules to reject wrong-product false positives.

Why:
- The most dangerous benchmark false positive is a plausible extraction from the wrong product page.
- Identity validation is distinct from field scoring and deserves its own explicit layer.
design:
Design Notes:
- Identity guardrails should fail closed on obvious mismatches such as accessory, replacement, compatible, bundle, or wrong-model pages.
- Model tokens and accessory signals from the dataset should be first-class inputs, not advisory metadata.
- The output should be reusable by scoring, escalation, and diagnostics layers.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- Identity checks can reject wrong-product pages even when extraction technically succeeds.
- Identity verdicts are deterministic, explainable, and integrated with content correctness evaluation.
- Known accessory and compatible-item counterexamples are covered by tests.
